(p-234) Sūrat al-ʿAṣr (Chapter of Time)

Imam al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "It is a chapter which, if nothing else had been revealed to mankind but it, would have sufficed them." This is the meaning of the words of another scholar: "It encompasses all the sciences of the Qur'an. Its purpose is to honour the human species, created from a clot of blood (ʿalaq), and to explain its essence and quintessence, namely the saved group on the Day when deeds are questioned for their purity. It does this after indicating their opposites, and it informs about what saves from deeds and states by abandoning the transient and turning towards the enduring, because it is the essence of existence and the kernel of being. Its name, al-ʿAṣr, is clear in this respect, for al-ʿaṣr (time/afternoon) extracts the essence of what is pressed and distinguishes its purity. For this reason the time of this final Prophet, who is the essence of creation, was the time of al-ʿaṣr, and the prayer of al-ʿaṣr was the best of the prayers. As for the explanation of its inclusion of the sciences of the Qur'an, it is by assigning its whole to [what] al-Ghazali said: The Qur'an is like a sea in which there are islands (p-235) with six kinds of mines, four of which are important. Two of the important ones are: a most excellent red ruby (yāqūt) for the knowledge of Allah, a green one for His attributes, and a blue one for His acts; and an emerald (zumurrud), green, which is the knowledge of the Last Day and what is in it. Two others are: first, a brilliant pearl (durr), which is the knowledge of the acts of worship that bring one near to Him, glorified and exalted be He; and second, a strong musk (misk), which is the knowledge of the customs through which acts of worship are prepared. Two complete ones are: a great antidote (diryāq), which is the knowledge of removing doubts, dubious claims and illusions, because they are poisons and destructive to religion; and a white ambergris (ʿanbar), which is taking lessons from those who perished by avoiding what caused their destruction, and following those who were saved by adhering to what caused their salvation. The first group is for the ambergris, because in it one smells the scents of the one who perished, and its opposite, the one who was saved. It begins with it because repelling corruption takes precedence over securing benefits. The second group is for the ruby with its three attributes, and the emerald. The third is for the pearl and the musk, which are acts of worship intended in themselves and customs that are extended as means to them. The fourth is for the antidote, because doubts and suspicions are only from vain illusions and false imaginings. The fifth is a means to it and completes it, because knowing that and avoiding it cannot be achieved except by exerting effort in patience." In the name of Allah, "Who, everything is perishing except His Face" (28:88); ar-Raḥmān, "Who has extended blessing to the righteous and the wicked alike, so nothing resembles Him"; ar-Raḥīm, "Who has specially granted the completion of blessing to His friends, so they became the forelock of time and the forehead of its people."

* *

(p-236) Since the pleasure of this apparent world lies in enjoying its goods, and since man is accountable for what he has witnessed, the chapter closed the matter of competitive pursuit of that bliss by threatening the sight of Hellfire. So the dweller of this abode is in the utmost peril, and his bliss is in the utmost turbidity. He said, indicating that most people are destined for ruin, emphasizing it with the oath and the particle because of the majority's denial of this, either by speech or by state: ﴿By time﴾, that is, the time in which the origin of mankind, Adam (upon him be peace), was created, which is the afternoon of Friday, as stated in the authentic hadith in Muslim; or the Middle Prayer, or its time, which is the time of the bearer of this Shariʿah (the sacred law), whose measure in past time is equal to the time of the afternoon of the day or part of it; or the time of each person, which is the essence in relation to him, as an alert to its preciousness, pointing to seizing the opportunity to spend it in good out of fear of the Gathering; or the time of late afternoon (aṣīl), because it is the best of it, by what it contains of freedom from occupations, meeting rest, and attaining the benefit of what one spent that day on; and by what it indicates of the length of the hour and the profit of one who had merchandise in it through concluding deeds and the end of the day; and it is the indicator of resurrection. Or it is the whole of time, in which Allah, glorified and exalted be He, brought the creatures into existence and decreed the decreed matters, by the wonders that appeared in it, which indicate the might and majesty of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, which calls for directing aspiration towards Him and confining it to Him. (p-237)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 103, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, mankind﴾, that is, this species, which is the noblest of species because it is in the best of forms, just as al-'asr (time) is the essence of time. Al-'asr is for extracting the essences of things. ﴿is surely in loss﴾, that is, in deficiency, according to their striving after their desires and their spending of their lives on their aims, because of their natural inclination toward the present, their turning away from the unseen, and their being deceived by the transient. The loss is general, whether it is small or great, according to the varying of people into the intelligent and the base. Whoever is a disbeliever is in kufr (ingratitude/disbelief). Whoever is a believer but disobedient is in loss, if he goes to excess in disobedience; otherwise he is in loss in an unqualified sense, which is the meaning of the bare verbal noun. In this there is an indication of the knowledge of the need for sending messengers to explain what is pleasing to [Allah] in beliefs, acts of worship and customs, in faith, Islam and their continuation, so that the one who does it is from the grip of the right hand and the one who abandons it is from the companions of the left.

Al-Ustadh (the teacher) Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase has diverted you﴾ [al-Takathur: 1], this contained an indication of the limitation of man's vision and the confinement of his perception to the immediate rather than the deferred, in which lies his success and salvation. That is because of his distance from knowledge of what the natural disposition requires. ﴿Indeed, he has been a wrongdoer and ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72]. He, glorified is He, informed that this is the condition of man by virtue of being human, so He said: ﴿By time﴾ [al-Asr: 1], ﴿Indeed, mankind is surely in loss﴾. So deficiency is his condition, wrongdoing is his nature, and ignorance is his innate constitution. Thus it is fitting that rivalry in increase should divert him, and Allah does not place upon him the spirit of faith, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Asr: 3], and so on to the end. These are the ones of whom Allah says: ﴿Neither trade nor sale diverts them from the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 37]. End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 103, verse 3:

Since a judgment passed on the species is a judgment passed on every individual, for they have nothing of their own essence except that, and since among them are those whom Allah, glorified and exalted, has purified from what man is disposed to, by making him in the best of forms and by preserving him from inclination, despite the deficiencies that are in him, He, glorified and exalted, made an exception of them, because they are very few in comparison with the people of loss. He said, indicating by the exception that souls are inclined to evil and given over to idleness and frivolity, that the sincere one is one in a thousand, as in the sound hadith: ﴿except those who believe﴾, that is, those who brought faith into existence, which is assent to what they knew by necessity of the coming of the Prophet ﷺ with it, concerning the Oneness of Allah, glorified and exalted, and belief in His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. Perhaps the wisdom of expressing it in the past tense is to urge entry into the religion even at its lowest degree, and to give good news to whoever does that, under its condition, of salvation from loss.

Since man is a rational animal, and the perfection of his animality lies in the practical faculty of movement by will, not by the compelling sensual appetite of the beast, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, that is, as confirmation of what they had acknowledged of faith, ﴿righteous deeds﴾, that is, this genus, which is following the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, in acts of worship such as prayer and in customs such as trade. Thus they were, by this, Muslims after having been believers, and they bought the Hereafter with the world, so the abundance of worldly things did not distract them, and they succeeded in eternal life and everlasting happiness, so nothing of loss befell them.

[Since man, after his perfection in himself through deeds, is not freed from absolute loss] except by perfecting others, and then he is an heir, because the prophets, peace be upon them, were sent for perfecting, and religion does not stand, and if it stands it is not complete except by enjoining good and forbidding evil, which arises from the light of the heart, and this cannot be achieved except through association. He said, singling out what is included among the righteous deeds to draw attention to its greatness: ﴿and enjoined one another﴾, that is, some of them charged others, by the tongue of state or of speech, ﴿to truth﴾, that is, the established matter, which is everything the Sharia has judged to be sound, so that nothing is valid in any way that negates it, whether of speech, deed, belief, or other, whether of action or abstention. Thus they were doers of good, and perfection in the practical faculty is by securing benefits.

Since man tends toward deficiency, the doer of that good becomes exposed to the hatred of the people of enmity, who are the majority in every age, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿and enjoined one another﴾, because man is stirred by exhortation, and both glance and word benefit him, ﴿to patience﴾, that is, arising from the purification of the soul in acting by obedience to Allah, including establishing the truth and nullifying falsehood and negating it and its adherents, and enduring what results from that of harm, by avoiding evils, until death, which is the cause that conveys to the abode of peace. Thus they were perfecting the practical faculty while preserving what preceded it of the cognitive. This is the wisdom of the acts of worship, for the wisdom of a thing is its purpose and the intended benefit from it, and here it is two matters: one external to the doer, which is Paradise, and one internal, abiding in him, which is the light brought near to the Truth, glorified and exalted. The expression by "enjoining" was chosen to indicate gentleness in enjoining good and forbidding evil, and the use of leniency to the utmost effort. Patience is the essence of man, his secret, his purity, his cream and his extract, which cannot be reached except by a man's pressing himself and compelling his soul to acts of obedience and subduing it to adhere to the Sunnah and the community, until patience becomes for it, through training, a habit and a craft. Its last part has embraced its first, and its joint has connected to its connector. (p-241) These are fourteen words, indicating that in the fourteenth year of prophethood there is permission for jihad, which is the head of enjoining good in action for the manifestation of truth, and this is the year of the Hijra in which its full moon was complete, its light and its worth spread, its might and victory abundant. If you add to them four words, the basmala, they become equal in number to the fifth year of the Hijra, in which occurred the Battle of Badr al-Mawʿid and the Battle of the Confederates, and in both the Prophet ﷺ displayed the utmost patience, then those who agreed with him among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, for the manifestation of truth and right. For at Badr they were forsaken by a caravan of ʿAbd al-Qays, or by Nuʿaym ibn Masʿud, and the hypocrites agreed with them, and they were frightened until terror and cowardice nearly overcame them all. So the Prophet ﷺ said:

"By Allah, I will go out even if no one goes out with me." And Allah revealed concerning it: ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith and they said﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 173], and the verses. At the Confederates, the eyes swerved and the hearts reached the throats, and the outcome of patience there was revealed in what the Prophet ﷺ said when they departed: "Now we will raid them, and they will not raid us." If you add to them the four pronouns, they point to the ninth year, in which was the Battle of Tabuk, the Battle of Hardship, because of the hardship that was in it, whose outcome of patience was the arrival of delegations, with the splendour of honour and fortune, and the continual succession of felicities, by the kindness of the Merciful, the Loving, and by that was the light of existence, and the continual flow of grace and bounty from the Worshipped God. And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, his family and his companions, the choice of existence.
